sources.entry: LibreKB - Web-based knowledge base solution. A simple web app, it runs on pretty much any web server or hosting provider with PHP and MySQL. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: LibreKB is a free, self-hosted, GPL-3.0 web-based knowledge base app written in PHP and backed by MySQL/MariaDB.
summary.what_it_does: LibreKB provides a web knowledge base with articles organized into categories that can be nested to any depth. Articles are edited with TinyMCE, with a configurable editor toolbar, and files can be attached to articles for readers to download. The admin area supports user management with predefined user groups, site settings grouped into General, Appearance, Editor, API, and Maintenance, and optional custom CSS for the public site. Password resets are sent by email. An optional read-only JSON API (added in 2.2.0, disabled by default) exposes articles and categories with GET-only endpoints, API key support, pagination, and search over titles and content.
use_cases: Host an internal or public knowledge base or help center
Publish documentation articles with downloadable attachments
Organize help content in nested categories
Expose knowledge base articles to other apps via a read-only JSON API
Run a branded support site for a project or business
how_to_run: Use PHP 8.4+, MySQL or MariaDB, and a web server honoring .htaccess; enable pdo_mysql, curl, mbstring, fileinfo
Put files on the server with the document root set to the folder containing index.php
Copy config.example.php to config.php and set database credentials and systemURL
Create an empty database whose user can create tables; make storage/uploads and storage/cache writable by PHP
Open /install, enter admin email and password, and run the installer
Log in at /login; delete install.php or update.php if present
notable: Runs on most PHP/MySQL web hosts, including shared hosting, and also via Docker
Read-only JSON API that hides the same articles and categories the public site hides
caveats: Requires PHP 8.4 or newer and MySQL/MariaDB plus a .htaccess-capable web server
Update checks were removed in 2.0.1, so updates must be checked manually
The JSON API is off until an administrator enables it
